Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,glob,re
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
def bgof(I): return Counter(x for r in I for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
# inspect each demo structure
for i in range(1,5):
    I=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); O=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} output'])
    b=bgof(I)
    si=[(r,c,I[r][c]) for r in range(len(I)) for c in range(len(I[0])) if I[r][c]!=b]
    so=set(O[r][c] for r in range(len(O)) for c in range(len(O[0])))
    posO=[(r,c,O[r][c]) for r in range(len(O)) for c in range(len(O[0])) if O[r][c]!=b]
    print(i,'in',si,'out painted count',len(posO),'colors',so, 'inp shape',I.shape,'out shape',O.shape)

# Look at the painted regions per demo: which cells got values, what value, and parity.
for i in [1,2,3]:
    I=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} input']); O=np.array(G[f'Demo pair {i} output'])
    b=bgof(I)
    H,W=I.shape
    po=[(r,c,int(O[r][c])) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if O[r][c]!=b]
    print('==',i)
    # count parities among painted
    import collections as C2
    p=C2.Counter((r+c)%2 for r,c,_ in po)
    print(p)
    # check: are odd-parity cells all one color? which color vs seed colors?
    seeds={int(v) for _,_,v in [(r,c,I[r][c]) for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if I[r][c]!=b]}
    vals=C2.Counter(v for _,_,v in po)
    print('seed colors',seeds,'paint colors',vals)
    # map paint color -> parity of cell
    for v in sorted(vals): print(v, [ (r+c)%2 for r,c,_ in po if _==v][:6])

def f(I):
    import numpy as np
    I=np.array(I); h,w=I.shape
    b=int(Counter(I.ravel()).most_common(1)[0][0])
    seeds=[(r,c,int(I[r][c])) for r in range(h) for c in range(w) if I[r][c]!=b]
    if not seeds: return [list(r) for r in I]
    rows=sorted(set(r for r,_,_ in seeds)); cols=sorted(set(c for _,c,_ in seeds))
    rs=min(rows); cs_min=cols[0]; cs_max=cols[-1]
    # vertical cyclic extent
    vert = list(range(rs-1, rs+2)) if len(rows)==1 else list(range(max(0, rs-1), min(h, rs+2)))
    # horizontal cyclic extent
    lo=(cs_min-1) % w; hi=(cs_max+1) % w
    horz = list(range(lo,hi+1)) if lo<=hi else list(range(lo,w))+list(range(0,hi+1))
    O=[[int(x) for x in row] for row in I]
    for r in vert:
        for c in horz:
            # find responsible seed: column parity
            # col cs -> rows same parity as rs; cols cs±1 -> opposite parity
            pass
    # assign colors per cell
    res=[[b]*w for _ in range(h)]
    for (rr,cc,v) in seeds:
        col=cc
        for rc in vert:
            for c2 in horz:
                d=abs(c2-col)
                if d==0:
                    if (rc-rr)%2==0: res[rc][c2]=v
                elif d==1:
                    if (rc-rr)%2==1: res[rc][c2]=v
    return res
